This study proposes no gate; the vocabulary is empty on both timeframes under the pre-registered rule (MDA log-loss mean > std AND top-8 stability), so under the frozen program rule the gate studies (gate_family, llm_round1, regime_gate) have no allowed feature columns and no allowed interaction pair. Re-opening the vocabulary (a calibration-free statistic such as the AUC drop, a calibrated learner, or a weaker rule) is a user decision that would be a new registration with its own sha and the multiplicity carried forward.
result.problems: 1) The null is partly a property of the pre-registered statistic: the depth-4 balanced-weight bagging is mis-calibrated under the |net|-weighted log-loss (worse than a constant predictor on both timeframes), so the clusters it actually splits on have negative log-loss MDA; the AUC-drop diagnostic (mda_diag.py, post hoc, no refit) would pass 2 clusters on minute. Reported plainly in FINDINGS as a diagnostic, not applied. 2) With most clusters at MDA <= 0, the per-period top-8 ranks admit exactly-zero clusters by default; harmless under the conjunction rule but the stability column alone is not evidence. 3) The tau rule kept 100% of rows in 12/12 (minute) and 11/12 (5minute) folds, so the full-model gate's kept-vs-skipped numbers are mostly undefined (bootstrap CI of the diff undefined on minute). 4) The 5minute finalize was not rerun: results_5minute.json was produced by the pre-split single-process run and already carries the revised harness.spa fields over the complete 53-row family; rerunning would only reproduce it. 5) Per-year stability re-scores the 12 fold models on each period's OOF rows rather than refitting per year (stated caveat). 6) Downstream consequence: phase3 gate studies conditional on this vocabulary have nothing to draw from; the orchestrator/user must decide. Nothing committed (brief: do not commit).
